title: Wire vector store as a CacheBackend + cache-engine composition (Repository)
description:
Route cache access THROUGH the Repository interface (lode-s2f.5) and resolve how multiple regenerable-cache engines coexist in the Repository's single cache slot. Deferred out of lode-x6r.3 (LanceDB vector store), which built the standalone VectorStore engine but did NOT wire it as a CacheBackend because doing so forces this composition decision before the FTS leg exists.

Scope:
- Make the vector store reachable via the Repository CacheBackend Protocol (index/evict -> chunk+embed+VectorStore.replace_vectors / drop), so callers reach vectors through Repository, not lode.embedding directly. This satisfies the 'access is through the repository interface' criterion that x6r.3 deferred.
- Decide + implement the COMPOSITION: the Repository takes one 'cache' slot, but the cache has multiple engines — passage vectors (LanceDB, x6r.3), the FTS5 lexical index (x6r.4), and later the networkx knowledge graph. Likely a composite CacheBackend that fans index/evict out to each engine. Settle this so x6r.4 (FTS sync-on-save) plugs into the same mechanism rather than inventing its own.
- Keep it the simplest thing that works (docs/stack.md 'keep the cache behind a repository interface'); record any settled composition decision in docs/ (stack.md/storage.md), not only code.
acceptance_criteria: Vector (and the FTS) cache engine is driven through the Repository CacheBackend; a composite/multiplexing backend fans head-change index/evict to each engine; callers reach the cache only through Repository, not the engine modules directly.
notes: NEXT-SESSION SEQUENCING (handoff 2026-06-23): build this SOLO and FIRST. It is the E3 lynchpin — it settles the composite CacheBackend that BOTH x6r.4 (FTS sync-on-save, now dep-gated on this) and the eventual E4 retrieval wiring plug into. Touches the repository.py seam + embedding.py/vectorstore.py, so it does not parallelize cleanly with other E3 work. The only safe sibling to fan out alongside it is lode-5y8.3 (golden Q&A set — disjoint files, but carries its own open metric-weighting question). title: Harden bd↔git sync: jsonl post-checkout hook reverts bd writes on rebase
description: REPRODUCIBLE: a bd close/label change made in a session is silently reverted when a later 'git pull --rebase' runs. Root cause: core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks; the post-checkout/post-merge hooks call 'bd hooks run', which reconciles Dolt FROM the working-tree .beads/issues.jsonl. 'git pull --rebase' checks out intermediate commits whose exported jsonl still shows the pre-close state (in_progress + ready-for-land), so post-checkout re-imports that and reverts the Dolt close. Hit 3x (lode-8bh, lode-wvf, lode-bxz). Contradicts the stated model (Dolt authoritative, jsonl passive). WORKAROUND that holds: after bd writes, 'bd dolt push' first, then export+commit jsonl once, then PLAIN 'git push' (no --rebase). Proper fix: make the flow Dolt-authoritative end-to-end — bake ordering into the producer/lander/coding agent defs + CLAUDE.md session-close (which currently mandates 'git pull --rebase'); consider ff-only pulls and/or disabling the jsonl→Dolt import on checkout. Blocks reliable landing — the whole landing loop rests on 'ready-for-land lives in beads'.
acceptance_criteria: A bd close survives a normal sync (no silent revert); the producer/lander/coding flows + CLAUDE.md encode a Dolt-authoritative ordering that doesn't lose bd writes; documented.
close_reason: import.auto disabled in committed config.yaml + CLAUDE.md rule; Dolt authoritative, jsonl export-only

title: lode add (capture + save)
description: Capture a note from CLI and persist via versions.save(); enqueue derive jobs. Instant, no AI in the path.
design: lode add = capture/create. Mint a fresh uuid4 note_id (logical id, no aliasing), read body from positional TEXT arg or stdin (verbatim; reject empty/whitespace-only). Open DB via init_db at --db (envvar LODE_DB, default ~/.local/share/lode/lode.db). Call versions.save() (always a create) — NO AI in path. On HeadConflictError write the rejected buffer to a unique draft file beside the DB, print 'note changed since opened' + draft path, exit 1 (never clobber/auto-merge). On success enqueue derive jobs (pending embed+enrich rows) via new thin lode.jobs.enqueue_derive_jobs in its own txn; reconciliation scan (docs/storage.md) is the self-healing net for the save/enqueue gap since the lane fence forbids editing versions.py to make it one txn. Lane: cli.py + test_cli.py + new jobs.py + test_jobs.py only.
acceptance_criteria: lode add captures a note and persists via save() with no AI call in the path, enqueues derive jobs, and on CAS reject writes a draft + prints the diff path.
notes: CAS-reject UX (CLI-first phase, since the interactive reconciliation UI is E11/TUI): on a CAS rejection, 'lode add' writes the rejected buffer to a draft file and prints the diff path + 'note changed since opened'; full interactive re-apply/discard waits for E11. Never auto-merge, never clobber.

title: versions.save() — CAS head, no-op dedup, op tombstone

design: versions.save() over the s2f.1 schema + s2f.2 hashing. Single primitive save(conn,note_id,body,*,parent,settings) that creates (note absent -> op=create, parent=NO_PARENT, atomic note+root-version insert via DEFERRABLE FK) or updates (note present -> CAS: parent must==current head). No-op dedup: body==head body returns the head, writes no row. delete(conn,note_id,*,parent) tombstones (op=delete, carries head body forward, CAS-moves head). recover(conn,note_id,*,target_version) repoints head to a prior version (no new row). CAS reject raises HeadConflictError(note_id,expected_parent,actual_head) — the clean seam s2f.4 extends into the diff/buffer-preserve conflict surface; NOT implementing that surface here. import content_version_id from lode.hashing (single source of truth).
acceptance_criteria: save() rejects a write whose parent != current head (CAS); a save with body identical to head returns the head and writes NO new row (no-op dedup); delete writes a tombstone op preserving lineage; head can be repointed to recover a soft-deleted note.

title: hashing.py — framed xxh3-128 content-address hash

design:
OWNS lode's canonical content-hash encoding — this is a STORAGE decision, ratified here, NOT by the eval seed fixture (see lode-5y8.4 escalation resolved 2026-06-23 -> option b). Beyond the hash code, two deliverables:
